meta.purpose: Damla's application-writing style, distilled from dewrites_verified.md, the Marx Finance letter session (2026-07-26) and voice memory. Every custom application letter must pass these rules.

process.owner: Damla is the SPEC. Claude asks motivation questions FIRST, drafts only from her seed sentences, she edits, Claude fixes only grammar and repetitions afterwards.
process.never: Never write a motivation letter without asking her motivation. Never invent facts (no 'I joined the session' if she did not).
process.after_edit: When she edits, report exactly what was changed and what was not, item by item.
process.before_writing: Read 1-2 relevant verified pieces from dewrites_verified.md, take rhythm from there, not from training-data letter templates.

structure.greeting: Dear Mr./Ms. {LastName}, (formal surname form; 'Hi {FirstName}' is too loose for first contact)
structure.p1_giris: Why I am writing (the application) + what I want (be inside startups) + the personal engine (hands-on experience for the startup I am building) + why THIS company in one sentence.
structure.p2_orta: Her story: what she has built (areas + concrete products), the gap turned into motivation, current work (one line), concrete LLM/shipped proof the announcement asks for, portfolio link.
structure.p3_kapanis: My CV is attached. You can search me on LinkedIn, GitHub or Google.
structure.length: 3 short paragraphs, never more. Kisa tutulur.

persuasion_rules.no_unsolicited_confessions: Never volunteer a deficiency that was not asked ('I missed the session' = wrong; silence is honest too).
persuasion_rules.single_gap_as_power: At most ONE gap, always converted to motivation with her pattern: 'I have never worked on X, and I fully believe that experience is what makes a person grow.'
persuasion_rules.confidence_first: Never 'I do not have X projects'. Instead '60+ repos, only X missing'. Power first, gap as a tail.
persuasion_rules.presuppose_the_meeting: Not 'open to discussion' but 'when we talk'. The meeting is assumed, not begged for.
persuasion_rules.own_startup_as_engine: Her strongest motivation line: gaining hands-on experience for the startup she is building. Founders respect founders.
persuasion_rules.match_their_ask: Map the announcement's explicit requests (e.g. 'mention LLM work') and answer each one concretely. If they say 'be concrete', give shipped products with one-line proofs.

banned_absolute: symmetric antithesis 'not X, it is Y' as rhetoric
allowed: numbers as natural brags (60+ repos, 70,200 drafts, 94.4%)
slightly broken, asymmetric rhythm (over-polish smells fake)
language_rules.voice: Flowing paragraphs, direct first sentence, no metaphors, real terms used when they carry the work (C++, WASM, benchmark), every claim backed by a number or a live link.

claude_known_failure_modes.note: Diagnosed 2026-07-26 from the Marx letter session (4 rejected drafts vs Damla's accepted final). Claude self-checks against these BEFORE producing any letter.
claude_known_failure_modes.1_no_motivation_material: The core material of a motivation letter is the writer's real want. Claude does not possess it and synthesizes plausible motivation instead (even fabricated 'I joined the session'). FIX: always ask Damla's motivation first; without her seeds, do not draft.
claude_known_failure_modes.2_writes_to_impress: Claude leads with the cleverest connection (analyst insight, pitch smell). Damla writes plain wants and beliefs. FIX: wants and beliefs first; clever bridges only if Damla herself says them.
claude_known_failure_modes.3_her_words_my_architecture: Even with Damla's verbatim seeds, Claude arranges them with rhetorical composition logic (confession stacks, contrast frames) and the text smells like Claude. FIX: keep her sentence ORDER and function, not just her words.
claude_known_failure_modes.4_pendulum_rule_lock: Claude turns each correction into a mechanical rule and over-applies it, deleting things Damla wanted (removed her agent-first confession after the 'no confessions' lesson). FIX: hold all constraints simultaneously; when two collide, ask which wins.
claude_known_failure_modes.5_assembly_without_intent: Claude assembles approved fragments and loses the letter's spine (once delivered a letter with no opening purpose). FIX: start every draft from 'why does this letter exist, what does she want', then place fragments.
claude_known_failure_modes.root: Claude writes to be evaluated well (polish, balance, safe cleverness). Damla writes to say what she means. Her roughness reads as trust; Claude's smoothness reads as fake.

sentence_mechanics.note: How Damla actually builds sentences, extracted verbatim from dewrites_verified. Imitate THIS, not native-polished letter English.
sentence_mechanics.openers: Sentences freely start with So, And, Still, Somehow, Then. 'So' is her most frequent connector, sometimes two sentences in a row ('So I needed a solution for that. So, I am building Rabadon!').
sentence_mechanics.chains: Long additive comma-chains that keep attaching clauses with 'and'/'so' instead of splitting ('the website talks to it through WASM, the test harness talks to it headlessly and can draft 2805 patterns at a time, and when iOS comes back one day it will not be a rewrite, only a new frontend').
sentence_mechanics.flat_break: CORRECTED BY DAMLA (26 Tem): she HATES the short dramatic punch sentence ('It never did.' / 'Then everything changed.') — that is LinkedIn beat-drop style, banned even inside a paragraph. A short sentence is allowed ONLY as a sincere statement of feeling or want ('I just love to be me.'), never as a rhythm device or emphasis hit.
sentence_mechanics.intensifiers: just, really, actually, even — used generously ('the imaginative work I actually wanted to do', 'making it really work with real needs').
sentence_mechanics.self_quote: Quotes her own inner voice mid-sentence ('hoped "this is it!"', 'kept calling it "progress"').
sentence_mechanics.repetition_unafraid: Repeats a word for rhythm instead of finding synonyms ('Still, even if... my pipelines still broke', 'my only friend, my only investor, the only one who believes in me is me').
sentence_mechanics.q_and_a: Asks a question and answers it herself ('So which one is true? All of them and none of them.').
sentence_mechanics.that_is_why: 'That's why I must speak for myself' — cause stated plainly with that's why / so.
sentence_mechanics.superlative_pattern: 'the hardest and the most important part for me' — doubled superlatives with a personal tail (for me).
sentence_mechanics.aside: Self-aware aside with 'but' ('It sounds a bit much, but I did all this just to make my own life easier.').
sentence_mechanics.closing_wish: Ends with a wish, slightly nonstandard phrasing kept ('I wish all the LinkedIn people creative and happy days.', 'I wish everyone building something gets to own the core of it').
sentence_mechanics.texture: Turkish-inflected English stays; do NOT nativize to perfect polish. Exclamation marks allowed when genuinely excited. Numbers sit inside the sentence flow. Rare CAPS for emphasis ('respect YOU').
sentence_mechanics.test: Read the draft aloud. If every sentence is balanced and smooth, it is not Damla. At least one chain must run a little long. And if any short sentence lands like a dramatic punch, cut it — that is LinkedIn, not Damla.

reference_letter_sent.text:
Dear Mr. Apaydın,

I am writing to apply for the internship at Marx Finance. I want to take part in startups not only for the internship experience, but to gain hands-on experience for the startup I am building. What makes Marx especially interesting to me is that it is agent-first, which is an area I have not experienced yet.

So far I have built projects in many areas, web and iOS products, C++ engines, ML tools. Now I want to learn by being inside such a different field. In my development journey, I have never worked on finance, and I fully believe that experience is what makes a person grow. I have been developing SaaS products, and right now I am working on an infrastructure project, a reliability runtime for AI-agent pipelines. On the LLM side I have shipped real things, a news product with an ML summarizer running in production, and a chat analysis product that runs my own model on the user's device. You can check them or see their progress on my personal portfolio, www.noseydewdrop.com. I am also publishing benchmarks for a few of my projects that have multiple different layers and engines.

My CV is attached. You can search me on LinkedIn, GitHub or Google.

Best regards,
Damla Su Bilge
